rationale: The document is relatively explicit about license restrictions ("licensed, not sold") but undercuts this clarity by using "buy" and "purchase" throughout payment sections, creating cognitive dissonance. The real consumer-hostile elements are the binding arbitration clause with class-action waiver and severe liability caps ($10 maximum), which together eliminate meaningful recourse for disputes.
evidence_quotes: The software is licensed, not sold, and Microsoft reserves all rights to the software not expressly granted by Microsoft
you and we agree to binding individual arbitration...not to sue in court...and may not bring class action lawsuits
your exclusive remedy is to recover...direct damages up to an amount equal to your Services fee for the month during which the loss or breach occurred (or up to $10.00 if the Services are free)
If you purchase a Service, then these payment terms apply" [but service is licensed, not sold]
Microsoft may at any time regulate, control, modify and/or eliminate the game currency and/or virtual goods as it sees fit in its sole discretion
